If your last safe-output call already performed the final requested action and no further work or tool calls remain, it satisfies this requirement. 2026-11-18T11:27:29.9080447Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9086959Z Safe-output calls are write-once declarations for real downstream side effects. Do NOT use them for probing, auth tests, retries with placeholder content, or "let me see if this works" experiments. If the task is complete but no real output is needed, call `noop`; if you cannot safely emit the intended real output, call `report_incomplete` with the blocker instead of trying variants.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9091278Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9095983Z **Tool retry limit:** if a safe-output tool (for example `push_to_pull_request_branch` or `close_pull_request`) fails, try at most 2 materially different recovery approaches. If the tool still fails, call `report_incomplete` with the error and the approaches attempted, then continue with other work. Do NOT debug underlying infrastructure after repeated failures.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9100003Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9106470Z **Trust successful tool responses.** Safeoutputs records write transactions that are applied after the agent finishes. A successful safe-output tool call means the transaction was accepted for downstream application. Do NOT independently verify the effect via `gh`, `gh api`, or other GitHub read paths from the current sandbox, because those paths will not reflect future safe-output writes.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9111939Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9115917Z **Do not inspect infrastructure internals.** When a tool or command fails, do not inspect Docker sockets (`/var/run/docker.sock`), mount tables (`/proc/self/mounts`), container networking (`/proc/net`), `/host` paths, git object storage internals, or container-runtime environment internals. These are outside your control; use `report_incomplete` after the retry limit.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9121556Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9132954Z temporary_id: optional cross-reference field only for tools whose input schema declares it, including create_issue, create_discussion, and create_pull_request. Do not add it to other tools. Canonical form: '#aw_' followed by 3–12 alphanumeric or underscore characters — e.g., '#aw_abc1', '#aw_pr_fix'. Pattern: /^#?aw_[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,12}$/i (the '#' prefix is optional; bare 'aw_abc1' is accepted and normalised to '#aw_abc1' automatically). Use this form in target fields only where their schema explicitly supports temporary IDs (item_number, issue_number, parent, etc.). In body/markdown text, '#aw_abc1' references are replaced with the real issue/PR/discussion number after creation. Omit entirely when not needed.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9141490Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9155447Z **Payloads**: safeoutputs tools do NOT support `@filename` expansion. For CLI calls, prefer a complete JSON object inline as one single-quoted shell argument. Inside JSON strings, encode newlines as `\n`, double quotes as `\"`, backslashes as `\\`, and apostrophes as `\u0027`; Unicode can remain literal. Stdin is also supported: `safeoutputs <tool_name> .` reads a complete JSON object from stdin — the entire stdin content must itself be valid JSON; never pipe a raw file or raw Markdown into this bare form. To pass one field's raw text verbatim with no JSON escaping, target that single field instead: `cat file.md | safeoutputs <tool_name> --<field> .` substitutes the field's value with the raw stdin text. Never write a bare `.` as a value inside a quoted JSON literal (e.g. `{"body": .}`) — that is not valid JSON. Do not use auxiliary shell commands or temporary files to construct payloads; the `cat file | ... --field .` form above is the one sanctioned exception, for raw-text fields only. When a native safe-output function is explicitly exposed, pass the fields directly.

2026-11-18T11:27:29.9184923Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9185362Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9185592Z To create a pull request:
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9186895Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9188763Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9192225Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9195180Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9197196Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9200259Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9201938Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9206603Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9211069Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9215447Z **Important**: `create_pull_request` is not a sandbox. Every successful call records a real PR intent that can become an externally visible pull request. Never use placeholder payloads like `"test"` / `"test"` to see what happens. If you are not ready to open the real PR, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.

2026-11-18T11:27:29.9378060Z

2026-11-18T11:27:29.9383520Z someone between chargers, so accuracy matters more than coverage: when in doubt, leave the data as it is and say

2026-11-18T11:27:29.9463072Z # Keep charging networks and prices current
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9463647Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9464051Z `networks.json` lists Australian fast-charging networks:
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9464910Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9466542Z - **How to recognise their sites:** `match`, lower-case text found in a site's operator or name.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9468408Z - **A typical price per kWh:** `typicalPerKWh`, with its `basis`, `source` and `checked` date.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9470277Z - **Whether an agent may read the network's own website:** `siteReading`.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9471144Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9472160Z `schema/networks.schema.json` describes every field. Networks price each site differently, often by the time of
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9474854Z day, and only their apps show a site's price. So a typical price is a guide, and drivers can set their own in the
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9476899Z app. This run has two jobs: find networks new to Australia, and keep the typical prices honest.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9478000Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9478218Z ## 1. Read your memory
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9478582Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9479555Z Your memory folder is `/tmp/gh-aw/repo-memory/prices/`. Keep one file, `operators.json`, created if missing. It's
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9481827Z a list of `{ "operator", "fastSites", "firstSeen", "lastSeen", "decision", "notes" }`. `decision` is one of:
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9483010Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9483273Z - `added`: you added it as a network;
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9484089Z - `alias`: it's another name for a listed network;
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9485554Z - `site-owner`: a business or council with its own chargers, not a network drivers join;
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9486995Z - `roaming`: its sites are run through another network's app;
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9488053Z - `pending`: not decided yet.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9488501Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9488713Z ## 2. New networks
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9489035Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9490052Z `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/sources/new-operators.json` lists operators in Charge Line's public charger file with three or
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9492211Z more fast sites (50 kW or more) that no network in `networks.json` matches. Work through **every** one not
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9494345Z already decided in your memory, largest first, in this run. Spend a few searches and fetches on each, not more.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9495958Z For each one:
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9496260Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9498049Z 1. **Find out what it is,** from the operator's own website (when its terms allow automated reading), Open Charge
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9499574Z    Map, government pages or The Driven:
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9500466Z    - a network drivers pay through its own app or card;
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9501637Z    - another name for a listed network (for example a parent company);
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9502696Z    - a site owner;
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9503313Z    - sites run through another network's app.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9504209Z 2. **A real network:** add it to `networks.json`.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9505222Z    - `id`: camelCase.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9505808Z    - `name`: as drivers know it.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9507195Z    - `match`: lower-case strings found in the operator names in the file, never one another network already uses.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9509344Z    - `typicalPerKWh`: only from a source that states the price (`basis` `published` or `survey`). Otherwise
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9510794Z      `null`, with `basis` `none`.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9512272Z    - `siteReading`: from its terms of use and robots.txt. Use `unchecked` if you couldn't tell.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9513666Z    - `source`, `sourceUrl` and `checked` (today).
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9515280Z 3. **Another name for a listed network,** or **sites run through another network's app:** add the operator's
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9516765Z    lower-case text to that network's `match`.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9517619Z 4. **A site owner:** record it in memory only.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9518205Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9519074Z **Deciding what an operator is** needs reasonable evidence, not a primary source: a government page, the
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9521132Z operator's or a network's own site, The Driven, or several search results that agree. Sites paid through
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9523206Z Chargefox's app, for example, mean the operator's text joins Chargefox's `match`. **A price** still needs a
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9524807Z source that states it.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9525178Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9526351Z **A network whose own site is blocked** (its terms forbid automated reading, like Exploren's) can still be added
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9527969Z from other sources, with `siteReading` `forbidden`.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9528616Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9528835Z ## 3. Typical prices
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9529189Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9530510Z For each network, look for evidence that its typical price has changed:
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9531390Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9531913Z - **The network's own website:** only when its `siteReading` is `allowed`.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9533746Z - **News of a price change:** The Driven, or the network's own announcements.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9535479Z - **Recent Open Charge Map listings** that state a price (checked in the last year).
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9536536Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9537710Z Change `typicalPerKWh` only when a source supports the new figure. Then update `basis`, `source`, `sourceUrl` and
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9543025Z `checked`, and give the old and new figure in the pull request. Keep `teslaPerKWh` and `freeKWhPerDay` up to date
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9545939Z the same way.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9546260Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9547149Z **When no source you may read gives a price,** and a network's `checked` date is more than six months old, open
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9549447Z an issue asking the owner to check the price in the network's app. One issue covering every such network.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9550649Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9550868Z ## 4. Propose
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9551160Z 
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9552060Z - **Changes to `networks.json`:** follow "Editing the data" and "The pull request" in the shared rules. Title it
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9555157Z   `[prices] ` plus a short summary, such as "Add Yurika; Evie typical 0.69 → 0.72".
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9558363Z - **Things only the owner can check:** open an issue. Three at most.
2026-11-18T11:27:29.9559663Z - **Nothing found:** propose nothing. Your memory is still saved.
